Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~41 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (CTO, AstraMetrics), Jonah Kim (ML Engineer), Ivy Zhao (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on PLG/self-serve Redwood API quickstart: time-to-first-token, free credits, onboarding flow. Customer evaluating Hosted for initial pilot and wants info on Dedicated/Private options for later. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, data retention, SOC2/KMS, and next steps to run a short benchmark.

Topics: quickstart experience, free credits, onboarding, token costs, Dedicated vs Private considerations, security/compliance, benchmarking plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm liam from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick round robin?
[00:08] Priya Nair: hey priya here, cto at astrametrics. we've got jonah and ivy on the call.
[00:12] Jonah Kim: hey all, jonah - ml infra.
[00:14] Ivy Zhao: ivy - devops. thanks.
[00:17] Sofia Patel: hi team, sofia, i'll be doing the technical parts and run through how quickstart works and follow up on benchmark ask.
[00:24] Liam Chen: objective for today: understand your current stack, success criteria, and how quickly you can hit first token with Redwood's hosted api. also map later Dedicated/Private needs.
[00:33] Priya Nair: perfect. our context - we build inference pipelines for observability signals, low-latency enrichment, internal tools. goal is POC in 2-3 weeks, production in q2. time to first token is important bc product team wants to demo.
[00:47] Liam Chen: got it. jonah, what does your current stack look like?
[00:50] Jonah Kim: right now we use an in-house microservice that calls openai for embeddings and completions. latency's okay for batch but for real-time enrichment we're seeing 400-600ms p95 which is borderline. cost is also creeping up. we evaluated aws sage maker endpoints but the management overhead got heavy.
[01:10] Sofia Patel: thanks. two quicknotes on redwood - our hosted api can get you to first token in minutes: sign up, apply free credits, create api key, curl a generate call. our quickstart has sample prompts, node/python snippets, and a small test harness. average onboarding for teams doing the plg quickstart is < 1 hour for basic tests.
[01:30] Ivy Zhao: when you say "hosted", where are the regions? we have data residency constraints for eu users.
[01:36] Sofia Patel: we have hosted regions in us-east and eu-west, with more coming. for compliance we provide SOC 2 reports and exportable audit logs. for stricter requirements Dedicated or Private VPC is recommended.
[01:47] Priya Nair: for the POC we can use hosted in eu-west, that'd be fine. later we might need dedicated pools or a private deployment. can you run Dedicated in our vpc?
[01:56] Marco Ruiz: yes, for Private we can ship a customer-managed control plane or an on-prem package; Dedicated can be provisioned with VPC peering and customer IP allow lists. there are tradeoffs: Dedicated gives you reserved throughput and predictable latency, Private gives full network isolation and allows keys to stay on your KMS/HSM.
[02:14] Jonah Kim: great. curious about cost delta - hosted vs dedicated vs private. and quantization - do you support INT8 or 4-bit?
[02:22] Sofia Patel: cost depends on utilization. hosted is usage-based (per-token), good for bursty PLG traffic. Dedicated is committed monthly capacity - unit cost is lower at high throughput because of reserved GPUs. Private has platform licensing plus infra. we recommend running a small workload profiling to estimate. on quantization, our runtime supports several quantization profiles and we can recommend per model; INT8/4-bit support varies by model.
[02:42] [02:45] Liam Chen: practical quickstart - we'll send free credits and a link to the quickstart org. the developer experience is: sign up -> create project -> get api key -> run sample request; we also have a sandbox model for fast dev.
[02:58] Priya Nair: about free credits, any limits? and is there a way to automate org invite?
[03:03] Liam Chen: credits are typically $X00 for POC accounts (we'll include exact amount in follow-up). we can invite your team by email or share an org invite link.
[03:10] Ivy Zhao: do you provide example terraform or k8s manifests for Dedicated/Private? we want infra as code.
[03:15] Marco Ruiz: yes, for Private deployments we provide deployment manifests and an ops runbook. for Dedicated we have terraform modules and guidance for VPC peering. we'll share those.
[03:25] Jonah Kim: security - SSO, RBAC, KMS integrations?
[03:28] Sofia Patel: SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC in console, and KMS integrations for key wrapping. audit logs exportable to S3 or SIEM. we'll attach SOC2 and our security datasheet.
[03:40] Priya Nair: good. next, latency: can you share p95 numbers for common models and seq lengths - e.g., 512 tokens seq?
[03:46] Sofia Patel: yes, we have perf profiles; for a 7b-ish open model on gpus we often see 30-80ms per token depending on batch size and KV cache. but for small single-token generation, end-to-end request p95 can be ~120-180ms hosted, depending on region. Dedicated typically improves tail latency. we'll include a perf spreadsheet.
[04:13] Jonah Kim: that 120-180ms is promising - current 400-600ms would be a big improvement. is streaming supported? we need partial results for UI.
[04:20] Sofia Patel: streaming is supported for generation and chat; we have SDK support in node/python and streaming via http/tsse and websockets.
[04:28] Priya Nair: any gotchas for time-to-first-token? e.g., cold starts, model cold kv cache?
[04:33] Marco Ruiz: cold start effect exists if the model variant isn't hot. for many deployments we use prefix caching and warm pools; for PLG hosted we keep popular models hot. Dedicated gives you pinned capacity. also compilation and kernel selection in runtime helps with variance.
[04:52] Ivy Zhao: how about data retention? logs or user data persisted?
[04:55] Sofia Patel: hosted default is short retention for request logs; customers can opt-in for longer retention or disable logging. for enterprise customers we offer options to prevent payload logging and to bring-your-own key with Private.
[05:05] [05:10] Priya Nair: ok, how do we run a short benchmark? timeline?
[05:12] Liam Chen: propose: we send quickstart + credits today; jonah shares a small sample dataset and priority prompts by monday; sofia drafts a benchmarking plan with a 1-day run, we run hosted and if you'd like we can schedule a dedicated trial to compare.
[05:26] Jonah Kim: sounds good. for sample dataset, it's small JSON lines with 10k records. we can anonymize.
[05:32] Ivy Zhao: we'll need an SLA for Dedicated - what does redwood promise?
[05:36] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and latency tiers for reserved pools. exact terms are in the enterprise contract; we can share sample SLOs.
[05:45] Priya Nair: procurement question - can we start with hosted POC and then switch to Dedicated without rework? how seamless is migration?
[05:53] Sofia Patel: that's a core design - same api surface and model catalog. migration often means switching endpoints/keys and adjusting routing policy; application code is minimal to no change. we do recommend validation and a canary rollout.
[06:07] Jonah Kim: what about model variants and fallback policies when a hosted model isn't available?
[06:12] Sofia Patel: smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants and region failover. you can configure cost vs latency policies and automatic fallback to cheaper variants.
[06:24] Priya Nair: any integration with our observability? e.g., datadog, prometheus?
[06:29] Marco Ruiz: yes, the console exports metrics and traces; we have tracing hooks and you can ship metrics to datadog via exporter. logs/audit export to s3 or SIEM.
[06:38] [06:40] Liam Chen: quick demo of the flow? i'd like to show the 3-line curl example.
[06:44] Sofia Patel: sure - (screen share) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-chat","input":"summarize: ..."}' - the quickstart repo has this exact snippet.
[07:02] Jonah Kim: and the sdk?
[07:04] Sofia Patel: node: import Redwood from '@redwoodai/sdk'; const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY}); await client.generate({model:'redwood-7b-chat', input:'...'});
[07:18] Ivy Zhao: how many tokens included in the free credits?
[07:20] Liam Chen: we'll include a credits note in the follow up; generally enough for initial POC tests and benchmarks - numbers will be in the email.
[07:28] Priya Nair: security doc timeline?
[07:30] Marco Ruiz: we'll share SOC2, encryption, and architecture docs in the follow-up packet within 24 hours.
[07:36] Jonah Kim: can you also share model card details and quantization recommendations for a 7b and a 13b we are evaluating?
[07:42] Sofia Patel: yes, model cards and recommended quant profiles will be attached.
[07:47] [08:00] Priya Nair: any constraints around rate limits during benchmark? we might want to run higher qps.
[08:05] Sofia Patel: for POC we can temporarily raise rate limits and coordinate with infra; for sustained high qps Dedicated is recommended.
[08:14] Liam Chen: ok let's recap next steps - i'll send quickstart + credits + org invite; sofia/marco will share security and perf materials; sofia will propose a benchmark plan; jonah to share dataset; schedule technical deep dive next week.
[08:34] Priya Nair: sounds good. one more thing: price ballpark for Dedicated?
[08:39] Marco Ruiz: depends on GPU type and commit. rough ranges: entry Dedicated package starts at $Xk/month for baseline reserved capacity. we'll include detailed pricing tiers in the follow up.
[08:51] Jonah Kim: thanks, this was helpful.
[08:53] Ivy Zhao: appreciate it.
[08:55] Liam Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.

End of call.
